acceptance_criteria.statement: A test case can verify an exact acceptance criterion content digest; changing the obligation leaves the relation stale until deliberate reassessment.

Implementation evidence exposes its canonical identity, role, pinned test revision, exact code references, optional stable step IDs and supersession history; outdated pins remain visible without rewriting evidence.

The explicit quality-runs query retains immutable legacy run identities, revisions, result literals, summaries, recorded command text, execution times, source identities, parent heads and evidence references as historical metadata only.
For compatibility, the deprecated run writer refuses a new record unless every current run head is named, without adding a run on refusal.
For compatibility, the deprecated run writer refuses missing test revisions or evidence references without adding a run.
A Roadmap feature can define a case using requirement links, preconditions, ordered steps and expected outcomes without code evidence; that same case and reader are reused after implementation.
An action or assertion can name canonical criteria and navigate canonical implementation evidence pinned to its stable step ID; manual and setup steps require no code link.

Adding implementation evidence preserves the stable case identity and current definition. Git retains earlier definitions; changed or reintroduced steps do not inherit stale evidence, and existing evidence pins are never silently advanced.

content.statement: As a developer preparing a feature, I can define how its acceptance criteria are verified before code exists and enrich that same case with implementation evidence so intent and verification remain traceable as the feature develops.
content.title: Define verification and link its implementation
